case_name: L. O. v. Mt. Lebanon S.D.

issues.label: Appellate jurisdiction and timeliness
issues.why: The court must confirm it has jurisdiction and that the District’s appeal from the common pleas order is timely and properly taken.

issues.label: Proper appellate scope of review
issues.why: The court must determine the correct scope (record review vs. de novo) and what legal errors it may correct in a local agency appeal.

issues.label: Standard of review
issues.why: The court must apply the correct standard (errors of law, constitutional violations, procedures, and whether findings are supported by substantial evidence).

issues.label: Agency adjudication status
issues.why: The Board’s decision must qualify as a valid local agency adjudication subject to review under the Local Agency Law.

issues.label: Certified record completeness
issues.why: The court must decide what constitutes the certified record and whether anything outside it may be considered.

issues.label: Supplemental reproduced record propriety
issues.why: The court must address whether Mother could file a supplemental reproduced record after the court ruled the certified record complete and what effect, if any, that has.

issues.label: Judicial notice of District policy
issues.why: The court must decide whether it may take judicial notice of the Residency/Enrollment Policy and notice provisions not introduced before the Board.

issues.label: Issue preservation and waiver
issues.why: The court must determine which arguments were preserved below and which are waived for being raised first on appeal.

issues.label: Waiver—burden of proof argument
issues.why: The court must decide whether the District’s burden-shifting/burden allocation arguments are waived under preservation rules.

issues.label: Waiver—multiple-district residency theory
issues.why: The court must decide whether the District’s argument that Section 1302 forbids “dual residency” enrollment is waived if not raised below.

issues.label: Cross-waiver by Mother
issues.why: The court must assess whether Mother waived arguments (e.g., 60-day notice policy violation or tuition-period challenge) by not raising them at the hearing/Board level.

issues.label: Remand vs. record limitation
issues.why: The court must determine whether additional evidence is permissible or whether remand is required/forbidden under Local Agency Law standards.

issues.label: After-discovered evidence standards
issues.why: The court must evaluate the legal standard for admitting after-discovered evidence and whether denial of the District’s motion was proper (even if not directly appealed).

issues.label: Effect of denial of evidentiary hearing
issues.why: The court must consider whether the lower court’s refusal to take additional evidence affected the correctness of its merits decision.

issues.label: Interpretation of School Code 1302
issues.why: The court must interpret 24 P.S. §13-1302(a) to define who is entitled to tuition-free attendance based on parent residence.

issues.label: Residency vs. domicile distinction
issues.why: The court must determine whether the controlling test is “residence” (physical presence) or “domicile/primary home” and how Pennsylvania cases apply.

issues.label: Legal test for minor’s residence
issues.why: The court must apply the rule that a child’s residence follows the parent/guardian and decide what facts establish that parent residence.

issues.label: Separated-parents framework applicability
issues.why: The court must decide whether legal standards for separated parents apply despite the Board’s finding that “this case does not involve separated parents.”

issues.label: Meaning of “reside” for parents
issues.why: The court must decide what constitutes residing in a district when a parent spends nights in two locations and maintains ties to another home.

issues.label: Permissibility of dual residences
issues.why: The court must address whether a parent may have more than one residence for school purposes and whether the law allows choosing between them.

issues.label: Physical presence sufficiency
issues.why: The court must decide whether Mother’s claimed overnight stays (about 10 of 36 nights) constitute sufficient physical presence to establish residence.

issues.label: Intent relevance to residency
issues.why: The court must determine how much weight intent to live in the district carries versus actual habitation and access.

issues.label: Access to apartment before keys
issues.why: The court must address whether residency can exist during a lease term when Mother lacked keys/access from Aug. 23 to Oct. 20.

issues.label: Effect of uninhabitable conditions
issues.why: The court must decide how ongoing construction, lack of gas, fridge outage, and child illness affect residency analysis.

issues.label: One-bedroom suitability factor
issues.why: The court must assess whether apartment size/bedroom count is legally relevant evidence of non-residency or an improper consideration.

issues.label: Utility usage evidentiary weight
issues.why: The court must decide what minimal electricity use proves (or does not prove) about actual occupancy and residence.

issues.label: Returned mail evidentiary weight
issues.why: The court must evaluate the probative value of “vacant apartment/attempted-not-known” returned mail and Mother’s explanation.

issues.label: Driver’s license address significance
issues.why: The court must decide how much the Pittsburgh address on Mother’s driver’s license indicates residence for school purposes.

issues.label: Mailing vs. service address mismatch
issues.why: The court must assess whether listing the Pittsburgh House as a mailing address on the electric bill undermines residency.

issues.label: Lease authenticity and effect
issues.why: The court must determine whether a signed lease and rent payments establish residency or merely an intention/plan to move.

issues.label: Renter’s insurance relevance
issues.why: The court must decide what weight renter’s insurance carries as proof of residency/occupancy.

issues.label: Furniture delivery invoices relevance
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether deliveries and furnishing show actual residence or preparatory steps.

issues.label: Post office change-of-address proof
issues.why: The court must assess whether alleged USPS filings and mailbox naming support residency and whether proof was sufficient.

issues.label: Vehicle garaging and auto insurance
issues.why: The court must decide whether changing garaging location and insurance address supports residence in the District.

issues.label: Photos at apartment relevance
issues.why: The court must determine the evidentiary value of photos showing children at the apartment for establishing residence.

issues.label: Security camera installation relevance
issues.why: The court must consider whether security cameras indicate occupancy/residence or mere preparation.

issues.label: Surveillance evidence reliability
issues.why: The court must assess whether limited surveillance dates/times and lines of sight reasonably support non-residency.

issues.label: Surveillance inference limits
issues.why: The court must decide whether not seeing Mother at the apartment on specific mornings/afternoons supports a broader conclusion.

issues.label: Behavioral therapist statement admissibility
issues.why: The court must address whether the therapist statement is competent evidence (hearsay issues) and what weight it can receive.

issues.label: Hearsay in administrative hearings
issues.why: The court must apply rules on hearsay admissibility and the “residuum rule”/competent evidence requirements for findings.

issues.label: Credibility determinations deference
issues.why: The court must decide the degree of deference owed to the Board/Hearing Officer’s credibility findings on appellate review.

issues.label: Common pleas credibility reweighing
issues.why: The court must determine whether common pleas improperly substituted its view of credibility for the Board’s.

issues.label: Substantial evidence review of findings
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether the Board’s key findings (e.g., 10 nights, lack of access, non-residency) are supported by substantial evidence.

issues.label: Consistency of Board reasoning
issues.why: The court must assess whether the Board’s conclusions logically follow its findings and whether it applied correct legal criteria.

issues.label: Burden of proof allocation
issues.why: The court must decide which party bears the burden to prove residency/non-residency and whether/when burdens shift.

issues.label: Effect of initial enrollment approval
issues.why: The court must decide whether District’s acceptance of lease as proof affects later burden or creates reliance interests.

issues.label: Due process—notice of hearing
issues.why: The court must confirm Mother received adequate notice of the investigation and hearing and a meaningful opportunity to respond.

issues.label: Due process—impartial tribunal
issues.why: The court must ensure the independent Hearing Officer and Board process satisfied impartiality requirements.

issues.label: Due process—evidence disclosure
issues.why: The court must consider whether Mother had fair access to the evidence used against her (surveillance notes/photos, returned mail, statements).

issues.label: Policy compliance—60 school days notice
issues.why: The court must determine whether District policy required a 60-school-day cure period and, if so, whether noncompliance affects the adjudication.

issues.label: Enforceability of board policies
issues.why: The court must decide whether internal policies create enforceable rights/remedies in a residency adjudication.

issues.label: Procedural regularity under Local Agency Law
issues.why: The court must determine whether the Board followed required procedures for hearings, record creation, and issuing findings.

issues.label: Adequacy of findings and conclusions
issues.why: The court must decide whether the adjudication contains sufficient findings of fact and legal conclusions to permit meaningful review.

issues.label: Definition of relevant time period
issues.why: The court must decide whether residency should be assessed as of enrollment, investigation, hearing date, or throughout the school year.

issues.label: Tuition liability start date
issues.why: The court must determine from what date non-residency tuition may be imposed if non-residency is found (enrollment date vs. determination date).

issues.label: Tuition liability end date
issues.why: The court must decide whether tuition can be imposed for the entire 2024-25 year regardless of any later change in residency.

issues.label: Change of residency after hearing
issues.why: The court must decide whether and how post-hearing residency changes must be considered (new petition, new hearing, or modification).

issues.label: Authority to assess tuition
issues.why: The court must confirm the statutory/policy authority for the District/Board to impose non-resident tuition and the method of calculation.

issues.label: Equitable considerations limits
issues.why: The court must determine whether hardship facts (domestic violence, inability to sell house, special needs) are legally relevant or cannot alter the statutory test.

issues.label: Domestic violence/separation relevance
issues.why: The court must assess whether estrangement and safety concerns affect residence determination or evidentiary evaluation.

issues.label: Children’s special needs relevance
issues.why: The court must decide whether special education/service needs influence residency entitlement or are legally irrelevant.

issues.label: Consistency with Section 1302 purpose
issues.why: The court must ensure its interpretation aligns with the statutory scheme preventing tuition-free attendance absent district residence.

issues.label: Whether common pleas applied wrong law
issues.why: The court must decide if common pleas used an incorrect legal standard by treating “one-third of nights” as sufficient per se.

issues.label: Whether Board applied wrong law
issues.why: The court must determine whether the Board improperly required “primary residence,” “domicile,” or near-exclusive occupancy instead of the correct test.

issues.label: Remedy on appeal
issues.why: The court must decide the proper disposition—reinstate adjudication, affirm common pleas, reverse with direction, or remand for further findings/proceedings.
